title: An Anchor Does Not Hold a Ship by Being Heavy

scenes.text: An anchor does not hold a ship by being heavy.
On a vessel weighing fifty thousand tons, the anchor might weigh ten.
That is nothing. It should skate across the seabed like a pebble.
The holding power does not come from the anchor. It comes from the chain.
Crews release far more chain than the water is deep, sometimes five times more.
Most of that chain ends up lying flat along the bottom.
Its weight pulls the anchor sideways instead of upward.
Pulled up, it pops free instantly. Pulled sideways, it digs itself deeper.
The anchor is not what holds the ship. The chain is.
